correctness.rationale: The mathematical series stated in the final claim has strictly positive and absolutely summable terms for d>1. Splitting m=1 produces the exact constant 64/(9π²). For each odd m>=3, (d−1)/(dm²−1) has positive derivative (m²−1)/(dm²−1)²; positive summation proves strict monotonicity without differentiating a nonuniform infinite series. Domination by m^{-2} after normalization proves both limits. Independent symbolic simplification verified the asserted rational partial fractions of 1/[m⁴(4−m²)²] exactly; paired odd shifts and ζ(2),ζ(4) give 5/16+π²/24. Independent values are lower 0.7205061947899575, upper 0.7237335167120567. This establishes all-d series identities, not a finite-truncation extrapolation. The claim that this is precisely the coefficient in the inaccessible primary manuscript remains a separately documented source verification risk.
residual_risks: The paper-defined PDE coefficient correspondence could not be independently checked from full primary text; only the explicitly displayed infinite series is completely proved.
No higher-order degenerate or non-diagonal transition is covered.
